home.heroSubtitle: Metamath Explorer is a visual, interactive companion to set.mm — the largest computer-verified library of mathematics — built to help you understand how a proof assistant works, one tiny step at a time.
home.sectionWhatBody: set.mm is a single, giant plain-text file maintained by the Metamath community since 1992. It encodes mathematics — from basic propositional logic to real analysis and beyond — as an unbroken chain of formal deductions, checkable by a program with no built-in mathematical knowledge whatsoever.
home.sectionWhyBody: Reading raw Metamath source is dense: cryptic labels, ASCII formulas, compressed proofs. This project decodes all of that into readable statements, cross-referenced comments, and interactive graphs — so the structure of formal mathematics becomes something you can see and follow.
home.featureBrowseBody: Navigate set.mm by chapter and section, exactly as its authors organized it, with readable statements and linked comments.
home.featureGraphBody: Every theorem rests on others. Expand a node to see what it depends on, or what depends on it, and trace a path back to the axioms.
home.featureLearnBody: A dedicated, interactive walkthrough explains constants, variables, hypotheses, axioms and proofs — with a live example you can step through.
home.featureLocalBody: No server, no account. set.mm is downloaded once and cached locally; parsing and verification happen entirely on your device.
home.footerNote: Metamath, set.mm and their contents are public domain. This explorer is an independent educational project, not affiliated with the Metamath project.

howItWorks.title: How Metamath works
howItWorks.subtitle: Metamath is deliberately simple: a handful of rules, applied with total rigor. Here is everything the verifier actually knows.
howItWorks.step1Body: A Metamath database starts by declaring its alphabet. Constants ($c) are fixed symbols like -> or wff. Variables ($v) are placeholders that can be substituted with any expression of a matching kind.
howItWorks.step2Title: 2. Floating hypotheses: giving variables a type
howItWorks.step2Body: A $f statement (a "floating hypothesis") declares the kind of a variable — for instance, that ph stands for a well-formed formula (wff). Nothing can be substituted for a variable outside of its declared kind.
howItWorks.step3Body: An $a statement asserts a formula as true without proof — it is either a fundamental axiom of logic, or a definition that introduces new notation. Everything else in the database must ultimately be derived from these.
howItWorks.step4Body: An $e statement is a local assumption: "suppose this is true". Theorems proved under hypotheses are conditional — like a mathematician saying "if P holds, then Q holds".
howItWorks.step5Body: A $p statement is a theorem together with its proof: an explicit, checkable sequence of steps, each one either a hypothesis, or an earlier axiom/theorem with its variables substituted for concrete expressions.
howItWorks.step6Body: Some substitutions would be unsound if two variables were allowed to become the same expression. A $d statement forbids that, ensuring substitutions stay logically safe.
howItWorks.step7Body: Hypotheses and variable declarations can be scoped to a block, so a proof technique or a local assumption only applies to the theorems that need it — keeping the rest of the database uncluttered.
howItWorks.verifierBody: For every proof step, the verifier substitutes variables into a prior statement and checks that the result matches exactly what the step claims — purely mechanical string matching against a stack. There is no understanding of "meaning": only symbol manipulation, applied with perfect consistency.
howItWorks.tryItBody: Below is a miniature Metamath database with two axioms and one theorem. Step through its proof to see the stack grow, shrink, and finally collapse into the proved statement.
howItWorks.stepperDone: Proved! The stack contains exactly the theorem's statement.
howItWorks.goExplore: Ready to see the real thing?

graph.title: Dependency graph
graph.subtitle: Every node is a statement; an edge means "is used by the proof of". Expand nodes to walk the dependency tree.

settings.title: Database & cache
settings.subtitle: Metamath Explorer works entirely offline once set.mm has been downloaded and parsed. Manage that local copy here.
settings.clearConfirm: This will delete the cached copy of set.mm from your browser. It will be re-downloaded next time. Continue?
settings.aboutBody: set.mm is fetched once from the official GitHub mirror and stored in IndexedDB. Parsing and proof verification run entirely in a background thread (Web Worker) using a vendored copy of google/metamath.js — no server is ever involved.

player.done: Proof complete — the stack now holds exactly the theorem's statement.
